<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par145 />is a substantival participle (''a lurker, a coucher''). In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=47|verse=24}} {{GHGheb|text=יִֽהְיֶה}} remains undefined in gender (masc.), although the noun precedes for the sake of emphasis; so also in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=28|verse=22}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=12|verse=49}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=28|verse=7|hidebook=1}}, 32, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=9|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=15|verse=29|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=50|verse=46}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=2|verse=7}} ({{GHGheb|text=הָיָה לִי}} as if the sentence began afresh, ''and servants born in my house... there fell to my lot'' this possession also). In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=20|verse=26}} {{GHGheb|text=לֹֽא־נֻפַּח}} may (unless {{GHGheb|text=אֵשׁ}} is regarded as masculine, {{GHGpar|122|o}}) be taken impersonally, ''fire, without its being blown upon''.—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=16|verse=8}} and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hb|chapter=3|verse=17}} the predicate in the singular is explained from the collective character of {{GHGheb|text=שְׁדֵמוֹת}} (see ''h'' above); on the other hand, the masculine form of the predicate is abnormal in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=87|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=2|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=12|verse=25|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=29|verse=25|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=8|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=36|verse=18|hidebook=1}}.<section end=par145 />

<section begin=par146 />{{GHGpar-heading|146|Construction of Compound Subjects}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|146|a}}
'''1.''' When the subject is composed of a nomen regens (in the construct state) with a following genitive, the predicate sometimes agrees in gender and number not with the nomen regens, but with the genitive, when this represents the principal idea of the compound subject.<ref>Sometimes, however, the attraction of the predicate to the genitive may be merely due to juxtaposition.</ref> Thus {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=2|verse=4}} {{GHGheb|text=קֶ֫שֶׁת גִּבֹּרִים חַתִּים|translate=the bow of the mighty men is broken}}, as if it were ''the mighty men with their bow are broken''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=26|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=13|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=1|verse=41}} (but the text is clearly very corrupt), 17:16, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=2|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=21|verse=17|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=8|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=15|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=21|verse=21|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=29|verse=10|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=32|verse=7|hidebook=1}} ({{GHGheb|text=רֹב שָׁנִים}} equivalent to ''many years''); 38:21; with the predicate preceding, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=10|verse=9}}, unless it is to be explained according to {{GHGpar|145|k}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|146|b}}
Rem. 1. The cases in which {{GHGheb|text=קוֹל}} (''voice, sound'') with a following genitive stands at the beginning of a sentence, apparently in this construction, are really of a different kind. The {{GHGheb|text=קוֹל}} is there to be taken as an exclamation, and the supposed predicate as in apposition to the genitive, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=4|verse=10}} ''the voice of thy brother’s blood, which crieth'' (prop. ''as one crying'')...!=''hark! thy brother’s blood is crying'', &c.; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=13|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=66|verse=6|hidebook=1}}. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=52|verse=8}} an independent verbal-clause follows the exclamation ''the voice of thy watchmen!''; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=10|verse=22}} and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=2|verse=8}} an independent noun-clause; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=40|verse=3}} {{GHGheb|text=קוֹל קֹרֵא|translate=the voice of one that crieth!}} i.e. ''hark! there is one crying'' is followed immediately by direct speech; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=6|verse=9}} {{GHGheb|text=קוֹל|translate=hark!}} may be used disconnectedly (cf. the almost adverbial use of {{GHGheb|text=קוֹל}} in {{GHGpar|144|m}}) and {{GHGheb|text=יְהֹוָה}} be taken as the subject to {{GHGheb|text=יִקְרָא}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|146|c}}
2. When the substantive {{GHGheb|text=כֹּל}} ({{GHGheb|text=כָּל־}}) ''entirety'' is used in connexion with a genitive as subject of the sentence, the predicate usually agrees in gender and number with the genitive, since {{GHGheb|text=כֹּל}} is equivalent in sense to an attribute (''whole, all'') of the genitive; hence, e.g. with the predicate preceding, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=5|verse=5}} {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּֽהְיוּ כָּל־יְמֵי אָדָם|translate=and all the days of Adam were}}, &c. (in 5:23, 9:29, {{GHGheb|text=וַיְהִי}}; but the Samaritan reads {{GHGheb|text=ויהיו}} here also); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=15|verse=20}}; with the predicate following, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=150|verse=6}}, &c. Exceptions are, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=17|verse=14}} (but cf. {{GHGpar|145|l}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=8|verse=25}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=64|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=16|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Na|chapter=3|verse=7}}.
